It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 1987.{{cite web |url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=December 4, 2020 |archive-date=March 16, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170316064243/http://congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |url-status=dead }} The district consists of forty six barangays of the city locally referred to as the "North District". It was represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by [[Rachel del Mar]] of the [[National Unity Party (Philippines)|National Unity Party]] (NUP).{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=December 4, 2020}} {{clear}} == Representation history == Since the creation of the seat in 1987, it has always been held by members of the Del Mar family. {| class=wikitable style="text-align:center;" |- ! {{abbr|No.|Number}} ! colspan=2 | Image ! Local: [[Kugi Uswag Sugbo|KUSUG]] | [[2025 Philippine House of Representatives elections|Re-elected in 2025]] |} ==Election results== ===2025=== Incumbent [[Rachel del Mar]] ([[Nationalist People's Coalition]]) ran for a second term. She was previously elected in 2022 with 45.99% of the vote and a 50,350 vote (20.65%) margin over her closest opponent. Del Mar ran against three other candidates, including Cebu City councilor Mary Ann de los Santos ([[Liberal Party (Philippines)|Liberal Party]]-[[Bando Osmeña – Pundok Kauswagan|BOPK]]) and Cebu City [[Liga ng mga Barangay]] president Franklyn Ong ([[Laban ng Demokratikong Pilipino]]).{{Cite web |last=Oliverio |first=Niña Mae C. |date=October 1, 2024 |title=Osmeña on Cutie's shift of alliance: Mary Ann is a better choice |url=https://cebudailynews.inquirer.net/597908/osmena-on-cuties-shift-of-alliance-mary-ann-is-a-better-choice |website=Cebu Daily News}}{{Cite web |last=Piquero |first=Pia |date=October 4, 2024 |title=Ong affirms 'very strong' alliance with Rama amid Ombud ruling |url=https://cebudailynews.inquirer.net/598587/ong-affirms-very-strong-alliance-with-rama-amid-ombud-ruling |website=Cebu Daily News}}{{Cite web |title=CEBUCITY1STDISTRICT |url=https://comelec.gov.ph/php-tpls-attachments/2025NLE/2025BallotFace/BFT_R7/CEBU/CEBUCITY1STDISTRICT.pdf |website=Commission on Elections}} Both Del Mar and Ong ran under BOPK in the previous election, with Del Mar defecting from her late father Raul's longtime party in favor of incumbent mayor Raymond Garcia's [[Kugi Uswag Sugbo]]. Del Mar won re-election, albeit with a decreased margin of 23,876 votes (9.56%), over second-placer Ong. {{Election box begin no change |
